help.title: Automotive Gage R&R
help.body:
Description
Automotive Gage R&R (Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility)

Purpose
Automotive Gage R&R is the standard AIAG MSA 4th Edition crossed two-factor study for evaluating measurement systems where multiple operators measure multiple parts multiple times. It partitions total observed variation into three components:
Repeatability — variation within the same operator measuring the same part (equipment variation, EV)
Reproducibility — variation between operators (appraiser variation, AV), including an operator-by-part interaction term
Part-to-Part — genuine variation between parts (PV)

The analysis uses a balanced two-way crossed ANOVA (Part × Operator) to estimate each variance component, then computes GRR metrics relative to the tolerance (product control) and historical process standard deviation (process control).

Inputs
Measurements (required) — the gauge reading for each combination of operator, part, and trial
Parts (required) — identifies which part was measured (typically 10 parts)
Operator/Appraiser (required) — identifies who took the measurement (typically 2–3 operators)
Reference values (optional) — known true values for each part; when supplied, bias per part is computed
Tolerance Range (USL−LSL) (required) — used to compute %Tolerance (product control acceptance criterion)
Target (optional) — nominal value; shifts the Probability of Misclassification plot x-axis to real part coordinates
Historical process std deviation (optional, strongly recommended) — used to compute %Process; without it the study variation is used and a warning is shown

Output Interpretation
MS Standard Deviation (GRR SD) = sqrt(repeatability variance + reproducibility variance). This is Macro's reported "MS Standard Deviation".

%Tolerance = GRR_SD × 6 / Tolerance. The primary AIAG acceptance criterion: below 10% is acceptable, 10–30% is marginal, above 30% is unacceptable.

%Process = GRR_SD / Historical_SD. Expresses measurement error as a fraction of true process capability.

Percent Contribution pie chart shows Repeatability, Reproducibility, Parts, and Other (process variation not captured by the study parts) as fractions of the total process variance (Historical_SD²). The "Other" slice represents long-run process variation beyond what the study parts represent.

Report Graph (optional) — two panels: measurements by Part (shows part-to-part variation with operator means connected) and measurements by Operator (shows operator-level spread). This is the primary diagnostic chart for identifying which components dominate.

Residual Plots (optional) — four-panel diagnostic: Normal Probability Plot, Residuals vs Fits, Histogram of residuals, Residuals vs Order. Used to verify ANOVA assumptions (normality, homoscedasticity, independence).

ANOVA Table (optional) — two-way crossed ANOVA with Part, Operator, and Part×Operator interaction. The interaction term tests whether operators measure differently across parts (a non-significant interaction, p > 0.05, is desirable).
